gloss: a lifesaver in a desperate situation; salvation in dire straits

definitions.gloss: a lifesaver when things look hopeless; salvation in dire straits
definitions.explanation: Literally "a Buddha in hell." Describes help, or a helper, appearing when one is in serious trouble with no way out. Stronger than an ordinary lucky break: the situation must be genuinely desperate.

examples.japanese: まさに{地獄|じごく}に{仏|ほとけ}だった。
{道|みち}に{迷|まよ}っていたら{声|こえ}をかけてもらい、{地獄|じごく}に{仏|ほとけ}の{思|おも}いだった。
examples.english: I was lost when someone spoke to me — it felt like salvation.

examples.japanese: {財布|さいふ}をなくして{困|こま}り{果|は}てていたところに{友人|ゆうじん}が{現|あらわ}れ、まさに{地獄|じごく}で{仏|ほとけ}に{会|あ}ったようだった。
examples.english: I had lost my wallet and was at my wits' end when a friend turned up — like meeting a Buddha in hell.

notes:
USAGE:
Most often predicative ({地獄|じごく}に{仏|ほとけ}だ / だった) or attributive ({地獄|じごく}に{仏|ほとけ}の{思|おも}い). The fuller form {地獄|じごく}で{仏|ほとけ}に{会|あ}ったよう is equally common, and the particle varies freely between に and で.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- まさに{地獄|じごく}に{仏|ほとけ}: a lifesaver indeed
- {地獄|じごく}に{仏|ほとけ}の{思|おも}い: the feeling of being rescued
- {地獄|じごく}で{仏|ほとけ}に{会|あ}ったよう: like meeting a Buddha in hell

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {渡|わた}りに{船|ふね}: a godsend — well-timed help, but the situation need not be desperate
- {棚|たな}からぼたもち: a windfall — unexpected good luck, not rescue
